data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/telemetry-emit.sh`. Reads `telemetry.endpoint`, `telemetry.client_id`, `telemetry.emit_excerpts` from config (or DSO_TELEMETRY_* env vars). Auto-populates 11 common fields from environment and config. Supports `--key <logical-id>` to register `event_id` in `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/event-id-map.json` (flock-protected concurrent writes). Supports `--link <key>` to populate `finding_event_id`. Enforces layer-a privacy (strips `cited_excerpt` to null when `client_id != "dso-self"` AND `emit_excerpts != true`). Hard-errors on empty `client_id` (exit 1). Maintains `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/telemetry-submitted.log` for idempotency. Submits via curl POST with fail-open semantics.
**Why**: This is the adapter every downstream DSO script (reviewer-dispatcher, future consumers) will use. Single seam for endpoint logic.
**Scope**:
- IN: The emit utility, idempotency log, event-id-map linkage, all three fail-open test paths.
- OUT: Reviewer-dispatcher wiring (separate story). AWS infrastructure (separate stories).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh` with minimal event-type-specific args produces a POST body containing all 11 common fields populated from environment and config, landing a schema-valid event in S3.
  ← Satisfies: sc-3  (sc-3: "telemetry-emit.sh auto-populates all 11 common fields from environment + config")
- When this story is complete, a unit test asserts the source and fallback behavior for each of the 11 common fields: `pr_number` falls back to null outside CI; `commit_sha` falls back to current HEAD when CI var is absent; `cycle` defaults to 1 when unset; `language` is auto-detected from `tool_id` or explicit flag; remaining 7 fields are always populated from config or fixed-value derivation.
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh --key foo` registers the generated `event_id` under logical-id "foo" in `event-id-map.json`; a subsequent invocation with `--link foo` populates `finding_event_id` with that `event_id`.
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh` with `client_id=test-host-project`, `emit_excerpts` unset, and `--cited-excerpt "verbatim code"` produces a POST body whose `cited_excerpt` is null (adapter-side stripping, layer a).
  ← Satisfies: sc-4  (sc-4: "privacy enforced at TWO layers: telemetry-emit.sh strips cited_excerpt at adapter")
- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh` with the endpoint returning HTTP 500 exits 0 and writes a warning to stderr.
  ← Satisfies: sc-5  (sc-5: "exits 0 even when endpoint returns 5xx, times out, or is DNS-unreachable")
- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh` with the endpoint TCP-accepting but never responding (simulated timeout) exits 0 after the configured timeout limit and writes a warning to stderr.
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh` with an unresolvable hostname (DNS NXDOMAIN) exits 0 and writes a warning to stderr.
  ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When this story is complete, invoking `telemetry-emit.sh` with empty `client_id` exits 1 with a clear error message.
  ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Concurrency] `event-id-map.json` writes must use `flock` (or `mkdir`-based mutex fallback) to serialize concurrent sub-agent invocations — parallel orchestrator batches will race on this file.
- [Idempotency] `telemetry-submitted.log` dedup is keyed by `event_id`; re-running with the same `event_id` must NOT POST twice.
- [Privacy] Adapter-side stripping is the first defense; never rely on it alone — Lambda handler enforces server-side.
- [Fail-open] curl flags must include `--max-time` and `--connect-timeout`; use `|| true` to guarantee exit 0 regardless of network state.
- [Testing] All three SC-5 failure-mode tests (5xx, timeout, DNS-unreachable) must mock the endpoint in CI; never hit the real Lambda.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a tool author, I want telemetry-emit.sh to auto-populate all 11 common fields, enforce adapter-side privacy, fail open on endpoint errors, and support cross-event linkage via --key/--link.
